entries.title: A plan-cap-deferred bead blocks its dependents and its parent's verify route until something reopens it
entries.summary: The plan-cap deferral (phases/plan.mjs) sets status=deferred and no engine code moves it back; only an agent reopen (reviewer reopenIds, planner) or a human does. Meanwhile classifyVerifySet requires every child closed and no unclosed 'blocks' prerequisite, so a deferred child keeps its parent out of the verify route and a blocks edge onto a deferred bead leaves its dependent unready.

entries.title: install --force stops a registered service via ServiceManager.stop() before any signal, and uses the pid delta to detect a supervisor relaunch
entries.summary: In runInstall's --force guard (src/cli/install.ts ~1740-1795), a registered service (registeredServiceManager()) is stopped with ServiceManager.stop() first. killApraFleet() runs only if every pid still alive was already in the pre-stop snapshot; any new pid after the stop is treated as a launchd/systemd relaunch, and the install exits with serviceStopCommand(). If the guard did stop the service, it prints serviceRestartCommand() and restarts the service right after the binary copy, unless the final service step will re-register and start it.

entries.title: The shared dispatch-role harness stubs out the watchdog, so timeout tests must re-wire the real one
entries.summary: createRecordingCtx's withDispatchWatchdog only records timeoutS/member/label and returns the dispatch promise unchanged, so any test asserting real watchdog timing through dispatchRole must overwrite ctx.withDispatchWatchdog with the implementation from dispatch-failure.mjs.

entries.title: Editing an apra-pm agents/schemas/*-output.json forces regenerating auto-sprint.js and the golden transcript
entries.summary: auto-sprint.js runs in a no-fs sandbox, so packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/scripts/gen-auto-sprint-schemas.mjs inlines each role schema (e.g. PLAN_REVIEW_SCHEMA) into apra-pm/.claude/workflows/auto-sprint.js, guarded by apra-pm/test/auto-sprint-schemas-drift.test.mjs; the schema text is also embedded in the dispatch prompts of test/fixtures/golden-transcript/mock-sprint-happy-path.jsonl, regenerated with `npm run update-golden` (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1) in packages/apra-fleet-se. Bumping a schema $id major additionally trips assertVersionPin in fleet-sprint/contracts.mjs.

entries.title: content[0] of a fleet MCP tool result is not the tool output; read text via resultText/toolErrorText
entries.summary: src/services/tool-registry.ts wrapTool() may put a user-audience <apra-fleet-display> banner before the real result (and a nudge after it) and never sets isError. fleet-sprint code must read result text through mcp-result.mjs resultText()/toolErrorText(), which skip banners. A raw content[0] read silently breaks prose checks such as vcs-auth.mjs provisionOutcome's leading-[FAIL] fallback, which is the live failure signal when structuredContent.ok is absent.

entries.title: StallDetector._poll skips live probes per entry by an adaptive cadence; tests must advance time past probeIntervalMs between polls
entries.summary: _poll computes probeIntervalMs = max(tickInterval, min(300_000, thresholdMs/5)), where tickInterval is the same STALL_POLL_INTERVAL_MS ?? 30_000 that start()'s setInterval uses, and probes an entry only when lastPolledAt is undefined or now - lastPolledAt >= probeIntervalMs. A skipped tick continues before both the probe and the stall-threshold comparison, so it is evidence in neither direction; a test calling _poll() repeatedly must advance the (fake) clock past probeIntervalMs between calls or the later calls silently do nothing.

entries.title: Generic-boundary guard scans EVERY string literal in fleet-sprint JS, not just prompts
entries.summary: check-generic-boundary.mjs scans all string literals (comments stripped) in fleet-sprint/**/*.{js,mjs,cjs} and all of apra-pm/agents/**.md, so even a thrown Error naming src/tools/*.ts or packages/apra-fleet-se fails the apra-fleet-repo-internals rule while the same text in a comment passes; fleet-sprint/skills/**.md is checked only for bead ids. A deliberate exception needs both an ALLOWED_EXCEPTIONS entry and a GENERIC-BOUNDARY-EXCEPTION: anchor comment within its window.

entries.title: Uninstall Kept-section dry-run must mirror the real-run deletion list
entries.summary: printKeptSection in src/cli/uninstall.ts hardcodes the dry-run planned-removal set; adding a new deleted dir to the full-uninstall global cleanup without updating it makes dry-run Kept output wrong.

entries.title: Every /mcp request needs a verified member JWT or the install's X-Apra-Fleet-Member-Secret header
entries.summary: In createHttpTransport, every /mcp request passes an auth gate before any session handling or registry lookup. A Bearer that fails JWT verification gets 401. With no bearer, the request gets 401 unless MEMBER_SECRET_HEADER (X-Apra-Fleet-Member-Secret) matches member-access.key in the data dir, which is re-read on every request. This covers full-scope and ?member= sessions alike, so test clients and packages/apra-fleet-client must send the header.

entries.title: provision_llm_auth structuredContent.ok is true for non-deploy outcomes; branch on reason
entries.summary: authResult sets ok = fields.ok ?? OK_REASONS.includes(reason), and OK_REASONS in src/tools/provision-auth.ts is ['ok','deployed_unverified','deployed_with_errors','skipped_local_member','stored_credentials_cleared']. So ok:true also covers a local-member skip (nothing provisioned; the host's credentials are used), a stored-credential clear, and a deploy with errors. A consumer that needs 'credential deployed and verified' must check reason, not just ok.

entries.title: kb_* tool description text is duplicated in generate-contract.mjs DESCRIPTIONS
entries.summary: Changing a kb_*/code_* registration description in src/services/tool-registry.ts also requires updating the hand-copied DESCRIPTIONS table in memory-contract/v1/generate-contract.mjs (and INVENTORY.md), then contract:generate; contract:check alone stays green.

entries.title: An armed watchdog's timeoutS resolves to the row's maxTotalS (hard ceiling), in both policy() and secondary()
entries.summary: role-policies.mjs resolveWatchdogTimeout sets an armed watchdog's timeoutS to timeouts.maxTotalS ?? timeouts.timeoutS, so the client-side kill uses the hard elapsed ceiling rather than the inactivity budget whenever maxTotalS is set. It runs in BOTH policy() and secondary(), because a secondary passing its own watchdog(...) in `over` replaces the already-resolved one; dispatch-role.mjs then resolves that budget name through ctx.budgets for withDispatchWatchdog.

entries.title: bd-replay matches per command string, not by sequence, and ignores unconsumed entries
entries.summary: replayBd serves each issued bd command from a FIFO queue keyed by its normalized command string, so reordering distinct commands still replays green and recorded entries that are never consumed are silently ignored; only issuing a command with no remaining recorded response fails, which means replay cannot detect a bd call that was removed.

entries.title: The bd npm pin has one owner: src/cli/beads-pin.ts
entries.summary: BEADS_VERSION/BEADS_PACKAGE live in the dependency-free src/cli/beads-pin.ts; install.ts imports rather than restates the pin, apra-pm/install.mjs keeps a copy held equal by a test, and ci.yml keeps an unguarded literal.

entries.title: An armed role watchdog races the row's hard elapsed budget (maxTotalS), not the inactivity budget
entries.summary: watchdog() stores timeoutS: null as a sentinel, and resolveWatchdogTimeout() replaces it with the row's timeouts.maxTotalS ?? timeouts.timeoutS (DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_S for most rows, INTEG_MAX_TOTAL_S / REGRESSION_TEST_MAX_TOTAL_S for integ/regression). It runs in both policy() and secondary() because several secondaries build their own watchdog(), so watchdog-timing changes must go through it in both places.

entries.title: Changing a fleet tool's zod schema or json result fails the client test unless the api.mjs JSDoc typedef moves too
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-client/test/client-server-typedef-parity.test.mjs textually parses src/tools/*.ts zod schemas (top-level keys at two-space indent), list-members.ts/member-detail.ts json result literals and several src interfaces, and asserts bidirectional field parity with the hand-written @typedef blocks in packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/api.mjs (RegisterMemberOptions, UpdateMemberOptions, MemberReservationOptions, KbExportOptions, ListedMember, MemberDetailResult, ...). It runs in the apra-fleet-client workspace suite, not root vitest.

entries.title: Changing which bd commands runner code issues invalidates mock-sprint bd replay fixtures
entries.summary: In mock mode (default npm test), bd calls routed through test/helpers/bd-replay.mjs runCmd are answered from test/fixtures/bd-recordings/<key>.jsonl, where key = temp-dir basename minus -<millis>-<pid> (e.g. apra-fleet-mock-sprint-<setup()/setupMinimal()/runDevelopLoopScenario() tag>), so renaming the test file is harmless but changing the tag is not. A runner change that issues a new or extra bd command fails with '[bd-replay] Recording drift' even though the test is untouched; fix by `node scripts/run-tests.mjs record test/<file>.test.mjs` with a real bd on PATH, never by hand-editing the jsonl.

entries.title: APRA_FLEET_MOCK_INSTANT_RETRY_BACKOFF=1 zeroes production retry backoff sleeps in tests
entries.summary: When APRA_FLEET_MOCK_INSTANT_RETRY_BACKOFF is '1', dispatch-role.mjs instantRetryBackoff() skips the dispatch retry backoff sleep (still logging 'waiting Ns') and git-sync.mjs mockInstantRetryBackoff() skips the post-dispatch sync retry sleep (still logging its delay). runDevelopLoopScenario sets it per scenario and restores it in finally; test/helpers/dispatch-role-harness.mjs sets it process-wide at import, so any test importing that harness runs retry ladders with zero backoff.

entries.title: command({failSoft:true}) swallows every non-cancel error, including a throw from a mocked execute_command
entries.summary: With opts.failSoft, WorkflowEngine._commandDispatch returns {ok:false, output:'', error:<message>} for CommandError, MemberNotFoundError and any transport rejection (wrapped as FleetTransportError), and {ok:true, output, error:null} on success; only CancelledError/ABORTED still throws. So a fail-closed throw inside a mock harness on a failSoft call (runner.js file-existence probes) surfaces as a soft 'not found' result, not a test failure.

entries.title: isTypedAbortError recognises pre-sprint refusals only by the 'Pre-sprint validation failed:' message prefix
entries.summary: fleet-sprint/abort.mjs isTypedAbortError has no instanceof PreSprintValidationError branch; its last line matches err.message.startsWith('Pre-sprint validation failed:'), so every PreSprintValidationError message raised in runner.js runSprintCycle (one per PRE_SPRINT_REFUSAL_REASONS value) must keep that exact prefix or the refusal stops being classified as a typed abort.

entries.title: Run a single test file through the bounded runners
entries.summary: Root: set APRA_TEST_SUITES_JSON to a JSON array of {name, cmd, args} (e.g. [{"name":"one","cmd":"npm","args":["exec","--","vitest","run","tests/foo.test.ts"]}]) and run `npm test` -- it replaces the default suite list but keeps the per-suite wall-clock bound and tree kill. apra-fleet-se: `npm test --workspace=@apralabs/apra-fleet-se -- test/foo.test.mjs` (args after the mode go straight to node --test, still bounded and sandboxed). APRA_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS overrides the bound.

entries.title: Every role-policies row must state resume intent explicitly because execute_prompt defaults resume:true
entries.summary: execute_prompt's schema defaults resume to true, which is a best-effort resume of the member's stored last session. That is why role-policies.mjs rows use FRESH_SESSION_RESUME rather than leaving resume null, and why dispatch-role.mjs resolveResumeArg never returns undefined: an omitted resume would silently reattach a one-off dispatch to an unrelated prior session.

entries.title: A regionBetween() anchor pair silently widens when the END anchor moves into a later module of the concatenated scan set
entries.summary: execution-role-dispatch-pins builds SRC by concatenating DISPATCH_LADDER_MODULES in order, so moving an end anchor into a phases/* module stretches a one-line region across every module in between -- and the test stays GREEN while measuring almost nothing.

entries.title: Never wildcard-bind a loopback HTTP listener; probe port availability by connect-then-loopback-bind
entries.summary: A wildcard server.listen(port) lets another process bind 127.0.0.1:<port> later and silently receive all loopback traffic, so createDashboardViewer binds {port, host, exclusive:true}. Supervisor isPortAvailable() first CONNECTs to the port, then falls back to a loopback exclusive bind -- never a wildcard bind, which triggers a Windows Firewall prompt that hangs headless runs.

entries.title: Tool zod .strict() is lost over MCP: server.tool(name, desc, schema.shape) strips unknown keys; only update_member is registered strict
entries.summary: tool-registry.ts registers tools with server.tool(..., schema.shape, ...), which the MCP SDK wraps in a non-strict object that silently strips unknown keys, so executePromptSchema's .strict() has no effect on real MCP calls. Only update_member is registered via registerTool with updateMemberSchema.strict() and rejects unknown keys. A schema's own .strict() matters only where code parses it directly, e.g. validateAgainstSchema in packages/apra-fleet-workflow/test/schema-validated-fake-api.mjs.

entries.title: Always open SFTP via openSftp: ssh2 1.17 sftp() leaks the session channel when the subsystem is refused
entries.summary: ssh2 1.17 Client.sftp() opens a session channel and on a refused 'sftp' subsystem request calls back with only an error, leaving the channel open and holding one sshd MaxSessions slot (exec() closes its channel). openSftp in src/services/sftp.ts compensates via closeRefusedSftpChannels, which ends matching SFTP channels from ssh2's internal channel table; never call client.sftp() directly, and run transfers through withSftpSession so each session is always ended.

entries.title: A src/tools/ function is not automatically MCP-server-only: src/index.ts routes subcommands straight into them
entries.summary: The register-member CLI subcommand calls the shared registerMember() tool function in a short-lived process, so lifetime/handle arguments that assume every execCommand caller is the long-lived MCP server are wrong.

entries.title: apra-fleet-se lint rejects compound 'orchestrator' identifiers in fleet-sprint/, bin/ and src/
entries.summary: test/backlog-role-no-orchestrator-identifiers.test.mjs scans every .mjs/.js line, comments included, under packages/apra-fleet-se fleet-sprint/, bin/ and src/ (skipping node_modules/ and docs/; only fleet-sprint/backlog-role.mjs exempt). It fails on orchestrator/Orchestrator/ORCHESTRATOR glued to an adjacent letter/digit/underscore (e.g. orchestratorVersion, ROLE_ORCHESTRATOR), roleMap.orchestrator, roleMap['orchestrator'], 'orchestrator member' (any case) or the text "orchestrator '"; the beads-member role is named backlog, so pick another name.

entries.title: dispatchRole resolves a dispatch's options INSIDE the git-sync bracket because the in-bracket claim step can narrow the streak
entries.summary: dispatch-role.mjs runDispatch builds agent() options (prompt, label, tier, budgets) inside invoke(), i.e. inside ctx.withGitSync, after running the in-bracket pre-dispatch steps (PRE_DISPATCH_STEPS_IN_BRACKET = ['claim-beads-batched']) and then opts.prepare. The doer's claim after the bracket's D-pull can reveal beads held by another sprint and narrow the streak, so hoisting option resolution before the bracket would dispatch the pre-claim scope.

entries.title: Supervisor shutdown never kills sprint children -- they survive as detached orphans
entries.summary: POST /api/shutdown and signals run createSupervisor's stop(), which closes HTTP and stops seams; the spawner seam's stop() only clears bookkeeping because children are spawned detached+unref'd and the ledger is the durable record. Stop a sprint via POST /api/sprints/:id/stop before deleting its directories.

entries.title: Bounded test runners reap nested detached process groups by SIGTERM cooperation, not SIGKILL
entries.summary: On POSIX both run-all-tests.mjs and apra-fleet-se run-tests.mjs spawn detached children, so the inner node --test group is unreachable from the outer runner; the outer runner SIGTERMs its group, waits a grace window, and the inner runner traps SIGTERM to reap its own group.

entries.title: Console /ext mount path reaches packages via a proxy-computed, spoof-stripped header
entries.summary: src/console/proxy.ts stamps x-apra-fleet-mount-path on every /ext hop and drops any client-supplied copy; the supervisor re-validates it fail-closed before interpolating it into hrefs and inline JS literals.

entries.title: Server bind port is resolved at call time: APRA_FLEET_PORT, then member-install marker port, then 7523
entries.summary: resolveServerPort() in src/paths.ts decides the port the http server binds and start/install check: explicit APRA_FLEET_PORT, else the port data/member-install.json records, else 7523; DEFAULT_PORT (load-time, env only) is no longer the bind source.

entries.title: beads-scope wrapCommand only invalidates on a command that RETURNS, not one that throws
entries.summary: The written invalidation contract says every beads-mutating command through the wrapper drops the snapshot, but the wrapper awaits rawCommand first with no try/finally, so a throwing mutation leaves a stale snapshot.

entries.title: Fleet tool failures come in three shapes; console isToolFailure misses prose failures, so they return HTTP 200
entries.summary: Tool handlers signal failure as structuredContent.isError (execute_command preflight, execute_prompt), structuredContent.ok === false (provision_llm_auth / provision_vcs_auth), or just a prose string (e.g. credential_store_update/delete '... not found'); a top-level MCP {content, isError} result is used by the code-intelligence tools. isToolFailure in src/console/routes/fleet.ts detects only the first two (plus top-level isError), so a prose failure falls through to the route's respond(): credential-store-update answers 200 echoing the request's metadata even for a missing credential.

entries.title: apra-fleet-workflow tests import the root dist/ build, so they need a fresh npm run build
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-workflow/test/schema-validated-fake-api.mjs imports the real zod schemas from the root dist/tools/*.js at module load, and npm test's pretest does not run the root build. Without a prior root `npm run build` those workflow test files fail to load, and after editing a src/tools schema they validate against the stale dist until you rebuild.

entries.title: Member kb_promote/kb_resolve_contradiction/kb_reconcile_prefilter need the engine kb_maintainer grant
entries.summary: The member tool allowlist is explicit (not prefix-derived): kb_setup and kb_export are never served to a member session (MEMBER_NEVER_TOOLS), and kb_promote, kb_resolve_contradiction and kb_reconcile_prefilter (MEMBER_MAINTAINER_TOOLS) are served only to a member session opened with origin=engine&kb_maintainer=1, which the engine opens (KB_MAINTAINER_CALL) for a repository's kb_maintainer. A new kb_/code_ tool is not member-visible until added to MEMBER_BASE_TOOLS.

entries.title: An async http.createServer handler that throws kills the apra-fleet server
entries.summary: src/services/http-transport.ts registers an async request handler with no outer try/catch and the server installs no unhandledRejection handler, so any throw in a route terminates the whole process.

entries.title: Windows dispatch completion is process exit plus a drain window, not pipe EOF
entries.summary: On Windows members, local and SSH exec settle on process exit plus a FLEET_EXIT_DRAIN_MS (default 2000ms) drain window, because grandchildren inheriting stdio withhold pipe EOF indefinitely.

entries.title: Adding a ProviderStats field requires editing memory-contract response-schemas.mjs
entries.summary: kb_stats returns {...ProviderStats, bible} unfiltered, and the kb_stats parsed shape is hand-declared in memory-contract/v1/response-schemas.mjs (emitted to schemas/kb_stats.response.json with additionalProperties:false), so a new ProviderStats field needs that zod shape updated plus npm run contract:generate. contract:check only cross-checks generated artifacts; tests/memory-contract-roundtrip.test.ts catches it only for fields the sqlite provider emits live, so an HttpKbProvider-only field drifts unnoticed (as degraded_* once did).

entries.title: Exec-level rolling timeout is per-provider via ProviderAdapter.execTimeoutSource()
entries.summary: The timeoutMs handed to strategy.execCommand() in execute-prompt is no longer timeout_s for everyone: claude/agy mirror max_total_s (or a 24h never-binds constant), codex/copilot/opencode/none keep timeout_s.

entries.title: Viewer SSE /events sends no headers until the first broadcast, so awaiting the http.get response hangs
entries.summary: createDashboardViewer's /events route calls writeHead without writing a body, so Node does not flush headers until the first broadcast. A test that awaits the http.get response callback before emitting an event deadlocks.

entries.title: getAgentOS defaults to 'linux', and getOsCommands needs the member shell or a Git-Bash Windows member gets PowerShell commands
entries.summary: getAgentOS(agent) returns agent.os ?? 'linux', so an unrecorded OS is silently treated as Linux. getOsCommands(os, shell) returns the WindowsGitBash command set only when shell === 'gitbash'; calling it without getAgentShell(agent) on a Git-Bash Windows member yields PowerShell command strings.

entries.title: A sync.remote URL outside SAFE_REMOTE_URL_RE silently disables the dolt remote-tip fingerprint instead of erroring
entries.summary: toGitLsRemoteUrl returns null for any sync.remote with no URL scheme or a character outside [A-Za-z0-9._~:/@+-]; null fails open to a real pull with no fingerprint and no error, so file:// temp-dir test fixtures must gate on that charset.

entries.title: execute_prompt checks detectUsageLimit after every parseDispatch and fails with reason 'usage_limit'
entries.summary: execute-prompt.ts's checkUsageLimit runs provider.detectUsageLimit after all five parseDispatch calls (initial dispatch, stale-session retry, overloaded retry, orphan recovery, trust-heal retry), regardless of exit code and before the stale-session/overloaded retries are considered. On a signal it records the session and returns structuredContent {isError, reason:'usage_limit', usageLimit:{resumeAt,resumeAtSource,message}, sessionId}. The workflow layer forwards usageLimit and sessionId onto AgentDispatchError.details unchanged.

entries.title: resolveFleetServerConnection auto-starts the shared HTTP server by default; stdio is opt-in
entries.summary: The client resolver uses stdio only when APRA_FLEET_TRANSPORT=stdio, or APRA_FLEET_SERVER_CMD/BIN is set and TRANSPORT is not 'http'; otherwise it attaches to the HTTP singleton or auto-starts it via autoStartFleetServer. It throws (never falls back to stdio) when TRANSPORT=http finds no healthy singleton, the singleton is alive but not answering /health, or the user ran 'apra-fleet stop'. It is not side-effect free, so do not poll it.

entries.title: Only scripts/run-tests.mjs makes scaledTimeout() scale; several comments citing concurrency 8 are stale
entries.summary: scaledTimeout() multiplies (x3) only when env APRA_FLEET_TEST_CONCURRENCY > 1, and scripts/run-tests.mjs is its only writer: TEST_CONCURRENCY (4, test/helpers/test-concurrency.mjs) for the concurrent lane but 1 for the SERIAL_PROCESS_TEST_FILES lane, so serial-lane files, test:slow and any raw node --test run get unscaled budgets. Comments claiming --test-concurrency=8 (scaled-timeout.mjs header, phase3 test) or that the var is inert under npm test (phase1 test) are stale: npm test goes through run-tests.mjs.

entries.title: kb_/code_ tool descriptions are hand-copied into the memory contract; editing one in tool-registry needs generate-contract + INVENTORY updates
entries.summary: Every kb_* and code_* registration description passed to server.tool() is reproduced byte-exact in memory-contract/v1/generate-contract.mjs (BASE_DESCRIPTIONS plus KB_SELF_NOTE/CODE_SELF_NOTE) and in INVENTORY.md Appendix A; bindings/mcp/<tool>.json is generated from it. Changing a description requires updating both copies and rerunning npm run build && npm run contract:generate; tests/memory-contract-roster-guard.test.ts and the contract:check drift guard fail otherwise.

entries.title: New fleet-sprint modules must be registered in GUARDED_MODULES or GUARD_REGISTRATION_EXEMPT
entries.summary: Every .mjs/.js file under packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/ (recursive, compared by full relative path) must appear in GUARDED_MODULES or, with a written reason, GUARD_REGISTRATION_EXEMPT in guarded-modules.mjs, or guarded-modules-coverage.test.mjs fails. Registered modules are scanned by the source-regex guards (dispatch-safety, dolt-literal, full-db-fetch, shell-command, unbracketed-push, explicit-id-create, inline-ladder), so extracting code from runner.js is not done until the new file is listed.

entries.title: Every fleet-sprint module must be registered with the guards, and shell-command-guard is a line-local, any-string scanner
entries.summary: guarded-modules-coverage.test.mjs fails unless every .mjs/.js under fleet-sprint (recursively) is in GUARDED_MODULES or GUARD_REGISTRATION_EXEMPT (with a reason). shell-command-guard.mjs then flags $VAR, ${...} in quoted strings, $(, ~/ and escaped backticks in ANY JS string (prose and Error messages included), so false positives need a '// shell-guard-allow: <reason>' on that line or the line above. It classifies quoting one line at a time, so expansions on continuation lines of a multi-line template literal are not detected.

entries.title: fleet.key path is resolved per call, but paths.ts FLEET_DIR and its derived paths are frozen at first import
entries.summary: fleetKeyPath()/getOrCreateKey() in src/services/jwt.ts call os.homedir() on every call, so a test that sets HOME first is isolated. In src/paths.ts, FLEET_DIR (APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR or ~/.apra-fleet/data) and the paths built from it (SERVER_INFO_PATH, LOG_FILE_PATH, SUPERVISOR_LOG_FILE_PATH), plus the env-derived DEFAULT_PORT and DEFAULT_HOST, are computed once at module load. A test must set the env/HOME before importing (or reset modules), otherwise it reads and writes the real data dir.

entries.title: Watchdog never auto-declares a live-PID sprint child crashed, by design
entries.summary: watchdog.mjs classifies a live PID that is plausibly the sprint's own child (--viewer-port marker) as running-healthy, paused, running-unresponsive (HTTP silent) or finished (terminal state in old_runs/), never crashed; crashed requires PID gone with no terminal state outside the launch-failed window. Late-failure visibility must come from the child's recorded terminal state, not by weakening the classifier.

entries.title: wrapTool may wrap non-JSON tool results in <apra-fleet-display> blocks; machine callers must not read content[0] blindly
entries.summary: wrapTool treats a result as JSON only if its text starts with '{' or '['. For non-JSON results it may prepend an <apra-fleet-display> onboarding preamble item and append a nudge item (both annotated audience:user) around the real text, so content[0] is not necessarily the payload; JSON results get neither. Programmatic consumers should use parseToolJson (packages/apra-fleet-client), which scans all content items.

entries.title: Supervisor router has no multi-segment wildcard, so /ui coverage is per-path
entries.summary: createSupervisor's route() compiles each :param to a single-segment ([^/]+) regex anchored ^...$, so a pattern like /ui/:rest never matches a two-segment path such as /ui/panels/git; registerUiRoutes must register every deeper /ui path explicitly.

entries.title: Supervisor sprint-row progress is pulled from each child's GET /state?summary=1, never recomputed
entries.summary: dashboard.mjs buildSprintViews() no longer computes progress from the supervisor's own beads clone; it pulls each child's published summary concurrently, classifies it (ok/unreachable/no-summary/unavailable), and caches the last good summary in memory per sprintId.

entries.title: Supervisor holds route matches registry UUIDs against ledger friendly names, so reservation holds never fire
entries.summary: The apra-fleet server's memberHeldCheck consults GET /api/members/:id/holds with agent.id (registry UUID), but reservationHoldReasons does a direct members.includes(id) against ledger reservations, whose members are friendly names (memberUnion of --members and roleMap). The reservation hold therefore never matches and the consult fails open; any fix must map id<->name on one side.

entries.title: kb_bible_commit removes bible entries the maintainer KB holds as superseded/invalidated and admits ids via kb_export's basis predicate
entries.summary: At every call (even with no ids) kb_bible_commit drops each existing bible entry that SqliteProvider.getRetirementReasons reports as retired (superseded_at set, reason from retired_reason with NULL->superseded, or content_hash='invalidated') and lists them in removed and the commit message; merely stale entries are kept. Requested CONFIRMED ids are admitted only through filterProjectBibleCandidates (bible-basis-filter.ts), the same predicate project-scope kb_export uses, else skipped as basis_mismatch/no_source_files. kb_export itself never removes entries.

entries.title: A supervisor test built without token/dataDir silently disables auth and passes vacuously
entries.summary: createSupervisor leaves token null when neither deps.token nor deps.dataDir is given, and the per-request guard is conditioned on that token, so guarded-route tests on such a supervisor prove nothing about auth.

entries.title: Reaping a reservation must use the returned post-write agent, and refusals must run before it
entries.summary: reapIfDead() (src/tools/member-reservation.ts) clears a dead-pid holder with updateAgent and returns the updated agent, so callers must use its return value: the pre-reap Agent object still carries the cleared reservation and would re-block the claim. Any refusal that must write nothing (e.g. member_other_owner in memberReservation) has to run before reapIfDead, because reaping is a real store write.

entries.title: runner.js may contain no phase() label call; each label lives in exactly one phases/*.mjs and the order is pinned
entries.summary: test/phase-sequence-order.test.mjs fails if runner.js contains any phase( call with a quoted label (/phase\(\s*['"`]/), requires each label fragment (e.g. phase(`Plan C) to appear in exactly its owning fleet-sprint/phases/*.mjs, and requires every phase module to be in GUARDED_MODULES. It also runs one mock sprint and compares the emitted phase() labels to EXPECTED_PHASE_SEQUENCE. Adding or moving a phase means updating the slicedLabels map, GUARDED_MODULES and (if the phase runs in the mock scenario) EXPECTED_PHASE_SEQUENCE.

entries.title: MCP-server ServiceManager.stop is a server.json HTTP shutdown, not a launchd/systemd stop
entries.summary: For the 'mcp-server' service (gracefulStopViaServerJson=true), MacOS/LinuxServiceManager.stop delegates to gracefulStopByServerJson (service-manager/index.ts): read server.json, POST shutdown, poll up to 5s, SIGTERM the pid only if it is verified as an apra-fleet process (else return false), then delete server.json. It never runs launchctl bootout or systemctl stop, so the unit stays loaded. The 'fleet-supervisor' service (gracefulStopViaServerJson=false) is stopped via launchctl bootout / systemctl --user stop instead.

entries.title: Three distinct git-credential-helper file shapes exist across member OS/shell combinations
entries.summary: The deployed credential helper differs by member OS AND shell: POSIX (linux/macos) writes an extensionless $HOME script, windows-powershell writes $env:USERPROFILE\...bat, and windows-gitbash writes a .bat under $HOME but is invoked through bash -- so any read-side builder needs all three forms plus the PowerShell call operator.

entries.title: Read execute_command output via commandResultStdout, not the 'Exit code: N' text envelope
entries.summary: execute_command's content[0].text is 'Exit code: N' followed by mixed output (CRLF on Windows); the clean stdout is structuredContent.stdout. fleet-sprint's commandResultStdout (git-topology.mjs, re-exported by runner.js and used by bin/cli.mjs's topology probes) prefers structuredContent.stdout, normalises CRLF and throws on a non-zero exit, so cross-member comparisons must go through it.

entries.title: A sprint has two identity strings: branch name for reservations and sprint_id, run-id for the runbook self-id line
entries.summary: bin/cli.mjs reserves members with sprintId: branchName, and runner.js tags every dispatch with sprintMutexId = args.branch. The 'own supervisor reservation id' line given to deployer/integ/regression prompts uses sprintSelfId = validated.runId || validated.branch, where runId is the supervisor-forwarded --run-id (effectiveRunId in cli.mjs). The two differ under a supervisor launch and are equal for a direct launch.

entries.title: memberHeldCheck is the combined member-held gate for member_owner and remove_member, but not update_member
entries.summary: memberHeldCheck (src/tools/member-owner.ts) merges the sync reservedBy check with workflowPackageService.consultHolds; a package's holds-call error fails closed (holds-unavailable) only for the owning packages passed in (current owner, plus the requested package for set), other packages' errors are just logged. member_owner and non-forced remove_member use it, while update_member's owner field only does an inline reservedBy check and never consults workflow-package holds.

entries.title: compose_permissions reports a refusal as normal text, not a throw or isError -- callers must check for the success glyph
entries.summary: compose_permissions returns denials (e.g. its NEVER_AUTO_GRANT denylist: 'Cannot auto-grant dangerous permissions ...') and persist failures as ordinary text results, not as a throw or isError. member-provisioning.mjs tryGrant therefore treats a grant as ok only when !result.isError AND the text starts with the tool's success check-mark glyph (COMPOSE_SUCCESS_MARK, U+2705); a try/catch alone would read a refusal as success.

entries.title: Project-scope kb_export is additive and basis-filtered, and refuses an unreadable bible; global scope rewrites
entries.summary: kb_export scope=project never removes or rewrites existing bible entries: it adds only CONFIRMED entries not already present whose source_file_hashes basis passes filterProjectBibleCandidates, leaves the file untouched when nothing qualifies, and throws (refusing to overwrite) if the existing .fleet/kb-canonical.json is invalid JSON or has no entries array. Global scope still rewrites kb-canonical-global.json from the live CONFIRMED set.

entries.title: gitRepos is an access list; only a single URL-shaped entry is a usable origin
entries.summary: agent.gitRepos is declared optional string[] and usually holds bare "Owner/Repo" access identifiers, not clone URLs. knownRepoRemoteUrl (in src/services/member-remote-url.ts, re-exported from execute-prompt.ts) returns a URL only when gitRepos has EXACTLY one entry AND it is URL-shaped (contains "://" or starts with "git@"); anything else yields undefined rather than a guessed URL.

entries.title: fleet.key is the member-JWT HMAC secret, so no console credential may be forwarded verbatim to a workflow package
entries.summary: getOrCreateKey() returns the HS256 signing secret used by jwt.ts sign and verify, so forwarding the raw fleet key upstream grants JWT minting; the console cookie and the /ext upstream credential are both derived digests, never the key.

entries.title: Member command env carries member.env only; decrypted credentials go through stageAuthEnv's staged file, and long_running wrappers get none
entries.summary: buildEnvPrefix/buildEnvAssignments (src/utils/env-prefix.ts) render only agent.env and skip names that collide with stored credentials. Decrypted credentials reach a synchronous execute_command or prompt only through stageAuthEnv's staged, self-deleting file, loaded after the prefix so auth wins. The long_running path writes buildEnvAssignments output into the persisted run.sh/run.ps1 with keepAuthNameCollisions and no stored credentials, so secrets never land on the member's disk.

entries.title: The dispatchRole engine must spell agent( and ctx.withGitSync( literally or the guards lose it
entries.summary: dispatch-role.mjs destructures agent from ctx so the guards' call-site regexes still match its one dispatch, while the bracket and watchdog stay ctx-qualified and are asserted by regex instead.

entries.title: serve.mjs must be launched via serveMain() without rewriting argv -- doing both double-boots the supervisor
entries.summary: packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/serve.mjs self-executes only behind isMainModule() (argv[1] === its own URL) and exports serveMain but no selfExecuting/main/run/default, so runWorkflow()'s trampoline (src/cli/workflow.ts, argv rewrite) cannot launch it. src/cli/supervisor.ts therefore imports serve.mjs WITHOUT touching process.argv and calls serveMain(passthrough) itself; doing both would boot two supervisors on one port.

entries.title: SEA staleness path list must include inlined workspace package sources
entries.summary: build-sea.mjs bundles src/index.ts with esbuild bundle:true, so workspace packages imported from src (apra-fleet-client, fleet-api-contract) are inlined into the SEA binary; their src and package.json must be in SEA_RELEVANT_GIT_PATHS, while their gitignored dist/ trees are invisible to git anyway.

entries.title: bd is invoked through two drifted exec-bd copies; change both
entries.summary: scripts/lib/exec-bd.mjs (root scripts) and packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/lib/exec-bd.mjs (supervisor; adds configureBdInvocation/resolveConfiguredWindowsBdScript for a configured bd path) both resolve bd on win32 via npm's bd.cmd shim and run node <bd.js> shell-free. If no shim resolves, execBdSync falls back to a {shell:true} win32 call with no argument validation (it carries free text), while execBdAsync always uses shell:true behind assertSafeArgs' [A-Za-z0-9_.-] allowlist.

entries.title: Review scope is built from engine-verified closedIds, not outcome status
entries.summary: reviewScopeBeadIds in phases/review.mjs unions each streak outcome's closedIds (engine bd read-back), skipping outcomes flagged publishBlocked or postDispatchSyncFailed. A failed or BLOCKED streak therefore still contributes the beads it closed.

entries.title: A sprint's own reservation is always in GET /api/sprints while it deploys
entries.summary: The supervisor ledger always lists the deploying sprint's own reservation, so a 'non-empty sprints array => stop' deploy gate blocks every sprint from deploying itself. Use classifyActiveSprints/isSelfReservation (src/supervisor/sprint-identity.mjs), which match self exactly on sprintId or integer childPid, never by prefix; scripts/check-foreign-sprints.mjs is the gate built on it.

entries.title: Only roles with a kb-apply post-result step record kb_captures; the KB block promises the channel only to them
entries.summary: A dispatched role's returned kb_captures is applied only if its role-policies.mjs row lists 'kb-apply' in postResult (today doer, doer-resume, reviewer, final-review, harvester). For agentTypes outside KB_SELF_INJECTING_ROLES (doer, reviewer), runner.js's agent() wrapper passes captureChannel=agentTypeAppliesKbCaptures(agentType) to kbInjection.blockFor/kbKnowledgeBlock, so other roles are told to note findings in their own report; an agentType shared by several rows counts as having a channel only if EVERY row has kb-apply.

entries.title: openSyncBracketCount is a pure aggregate counter; cross-owner bracket overlap is legitimate except the opt-in code-write key
entries.summary: git-sync.mjs createSyncBrackets counts open brackets with no owner awareness; overlap across members is legitimate by default (D-push is serialized by the dolt push mutex). Only brackets passing exclusiveKey (CODE_WRITE_BRACKET_KEY, used by pushCode:true withGitSync) are tracked on a per-key stack and throw ConcurrentSyncBracketError on a crossing close. What keeps code-writing dispatches from overlapping is the globalDoerTurn FIFO gate in phases/develop.mjs; the exclusive key is a backstop for it being broken.

entries.title: VCS provider builders pick the curl binary by os and the quoting dialect by shell
entries.summary: In the fleet-sprint VCS provider builders, os picks the curl BINARY (curlBinary: curl.exe on windows) and shell picks the QUOTING dialect (shQuote via usesPowerShellQuoting: gitbash is POSIX, pwsh7/powershell5 are PowerShell, otherwise it falls back to os). A windows+gitbash member therefore gets curl.exe with POSIX quoting, and callers must pass both os and shell from resolveMemberTarget.

entries.title: Moving a command() call site out of runner.js breaks the runner.js command-count baseline
entries.summary: test/dispatch-safety-guard.test.mjs asserts exact counts with strictEqual: EXPECTED_COMMAND_COUNT (command() sites in runner.js) and EXPECTED_AGENT_COUNT (agent() sites, 0), plus EXPECTED_<MODULE>_COMMAND_COUNT for many extracted modules (e.g. EXPECTED_VCS_AUTH_COMMAND_COUNT). A move-only extraction must decrement the runner count, update or add the destination module's baseline, and register the new file in fleet-sprint/guarded-modules.mjs.

entries.title: Adding any duplicated top-level string to viewer state can turn plain /state fields into $ref markers
entries.summary: buildListStatePayload() dedupes every string of 24+ chars that occurs 2+ times anywhere in the payload, top-level fields included, into {$ref:n} plus a _strings table. Copying runId or ISO timestamps into a new top-level state object turns state.runId etc. into $ref markers for /state consumers that do not call resolveStringRefs; the /state handler already pulls `summary` out of state and re-attaches it after dedupe for this reason -- do the same for any new top-level object.

entries.title: Supervisor token is fixed at boot; fleet.key (always under os.homedir) can appear later and diverge
entries.summary: resolveServiceToken() (readLocalToken) prefers os.homedir()/.apra-fleet/fleet.key -- ignoring APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR, so sandboxes share the operator's real key -- else <dataDir>/private/token, and bin/serve.mjs resolves it once at boot. fleet.key is minted by apra-fleet install and lazily by the server's getOrCreateKey(), never by apra-fleet start, so a later re-resolve can return fleet.key while the running supervisor still expects private/token (HTTP 401); probes should use createIfMissing:false and re-check the source they proved.

entries.title: A blocks edge inside a streak lane splits the lane instead of sequencing it
entries.summary: groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata groups only the CURRENT ready set, so a blocks edge between two beads sharing a metadata.streak keeps the blocked one out of the ready set and the lane is split into separate review rounds. Order work within a lane with streakOrder; use blocks only between different lanes.

entries.title: retry.infraResumeAttempts is a boolean gate, not a count -- a value above 1 is silently ignored
entries.summary: dispatchRole reads retry.infraResumeAttempts only as `> 0`; on an infra failure the resume loop runs Math.max(retry.resumeAttempts, 1) times, so the field's magnitude never matters. A resume that fails with another infra error is rethrown -- the loop only continues on a repeated max_turns exhaustion (with maxTurnsResume) or on session_not_found, which falls back to a fresh full-prompt session without charging the ladder.

entries.title: SSH host-key mismatch is auto-accepted (TOFU) and only logged
entries.summary: connectWithTOFU (src/services/ssh.ts) catches HostKeyMismatchError, overwrites the known_hosts entry via replaceKnownHost, drops the pooled connection and reconnects once. The change shows up only as a logWarn and a returned warning, which execCommand prepends to stderr and SFTP transfers drop, so a changed host key by itself never fails the call.

entries.title: The ASCII-only gate fails on shrink, so baselining generated files is a trap
entries.summary: check-ascii-only.mjs evaluate() fails on new-file, ratchet AND shrink findings; a baselined file that loses non-ASCII characters (or is deleted) turns npm test red until ascii-baseline.mjs is edited, and .beads/issues.jsonl is baselined even though bd regenerates it.

entries.title: degrade.classes, not degrade.kind, decides what a ladder fabricates -- the integ runner omits 'infra' so an envelope-less failure is INCONCLUSIVE, not passed:false
entries.summary: synthesizeDegradedValue fabricates a value only for error classes listed in the row's degrade.classes. The integ-test-runner row lists schema and dispatch but not infra; together with classifiesInfraFailures:true (which makes the 'infra' class reachable) and kind 'inconclusive' (which makes inconclusiveOf return a record), an envelope-less member failure yields an inconclusive record instead of a fabricated passed:false report.

entries.title: vitest injects __dirname, so typeof __dirname dual-path code takes the CJS branch in tests
entries.summary: Under vitest, modules like src/console/static.ts see a defined __dirname, so resolveDefaultShellDistDir() takes the CJS/SEA branch in-process; plain node -e (CJS eval) also defines __dirname/require globals. Only a real ES-module child exercises the ESM branch.

entries.title: The supervisor pins its own api-guard token at startup and never re-reads it
entries.summary: bin/serve.mjs resolves the credential guarding its own HTTP surface exactly once at boot, so a supervisor started before fleet.key exists rejects fleet-key bearers for its whole life.

entries.title: test/helpers/dispatch-pin-scanner.mjs has its own maskComments that does not model regex literals
entries.summary: The regex-literal desync fixed in fleet-sprint/dispatch-safety-guard.mjs still exists in the pin scanner's own maskComments, which drives the dispatch-pin and role-policy census tests; it is latent until a quote-bearing regex lands in a DISPATCH_LADDER_MODULES file.

entries.title: Every /mcp request on an existing session id is bound to the identity that opened it
entries.summary: http-transport records a SessionOwner (jwt memberId+workspaceId, or access secret) at initialize and refuses GET/DELETE/non-initialize POST from any other identity with 403 'session identity mismatch'; any access-secret caller may use any secret-opened session regardless of ?member=.

entries.title: ESM main-module guard must use pathToFileURL, not string interpolation, or it silently no-ops on win32
entries.summary: Comparing import.meta.url to a template-literal file:// string built from process.argv[1] is always false on Windows, so main() never runs -- no crash, just a silent exit 0.

entries.title: Windows local-member child env is bounded by boundChildEnv (deduped PATH, 32767-char cap)
entries.summary: WindowsCommands.getCleanEnv and WindowsGitBashCommands.cleanExec pass their env through boundChildEnv (src/os/child-env-bound.ts): PATH deduped case-insensitively, and the largest non-protected vars dropped until the block fits CHILD_ENV_BLOCK_CAP_CHARS.

entries.title: dolt-sync.mjs sync.remote/tip memoization is process-lifetime, so multi-scenario tests must reset it between runs
entries.summary: fleet-sprint/dolt-sync.mjs keeps each member's sync.remote answer (syncRemoteCache), last-synced tip fingerprint and tip-probe failures in module-level Maps that survive across sprint runs in one process (only hard seams or the exported reset functions clear them). So the first mock-sprint scenario in a process issues probes that later ones skip; tests comparing two runs in one process must call invalidateSyncRemoteCache(), clearLastSyncedTip() and clearTipProbeFailures() between them.

entries.title: SqliteProvider freshness verdicts must be suppressed, not re-hashed, when the repo anchor is unreachable
entries.summary: A repo_path that does not exist on this host (the remote-member case) must never fall back to process.cwd() as the freshness anchor, and must not be re-hashed against it either -- both checkFreshness and freshnessSweep now short-circuit to a no-op verdict via a shared anchorIsMissing() check instead.

entries.title: The sprint runner's dispatch inactivity budget is clamped to 1800s and differs from max_total_s
entries.summary: runner.js computes DISPATCH_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_S = resolveDispatchInactivityTimeoutS(DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_S) = min(1800, dispatch_timeout_s), while most role rows use DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_S itself as maxTotalS (integ/regression use longer INTEG_MAX_TOTAL_S / REGRESSION_TEST_MAX_TOTAL_S). With the default dispatch_timeout_s of 9000 the two budgets always diverge, so code or comments assuming timeout_s == max_total_s are wrong.

entries.title: Provider-conditional body markers must be on their own line and cannot be quoted inside a fence
entries.summary: CONDITIONAL_MARKER_RE eats surrounding whitespace without requiring an own-line marker, and the resolver has no fence awareness.

entries.title: vcs_credential_exec has two token placeholders with opposite quoting contracts, and mixing them up surfaces as a false 401
entries.summary: The bare vcs_token placeholder is substituted already quoted; the vcs_token_inline placeholder gets interior-only escaping for use inside caller quotes. Picking the wrong one double-escapes or leaves the token unquoted.

entries.title: Supervisor guard accepts three distinct credentials, each on one channel only
entries.summary: isAuthorized accepts the raw service token only as a Bearer header, deriveUpstreamCredential(token, PACKAGE_ID='se') only as a Bearer header (the /ext/se proxy hop), and deriveDashboardCookie(token) only on the se_token cookie. Browsers get that cookie via handleTokenExchange: a ?token=<raw> page request sets the derived cookie and 302s with the token stripped.

entries.title: Dashboard helpers are shipped to the browser via .toString() and must be self-contained
entries.summary: Renderers/helpers used by the supervisor dashboard (escapeHtml, renderSprintSection, formatSummaryAge, mountHref from mount-prefix.mjs, ...) are inlined into client scripts like sprintStackLiveScript() via fn.toString(), so their bodies may not reference module-level bindings or imports (pass values such as mountPrefix explicitly), and every helper they call must also be embedded in the same script. supervisor-dashboard-live-refresh.test.mjs executes the script and fails when an embedded renderer references a non-embedded helper or drifts from the module copy.

entries.title: The service token reaches a runner only through spawner env injection, never through argv or a file read
entries.summary: coordination.mjs's clients resolve the token as opts.token ?? process.env.FLEET_SE_SERVICE_TOKEN, and only spawner.mjs sets that env var, so a runner started outside the supervisor's spawner has no credential for the guarded coordination routes.

entries.title: Usage-limit pause budget resets per onUsageLimit call, and a usage-limit re-dispatch is not charged to the retry ladder
entries.summary: createUsageLimitPauseController's USAGE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_S / MAX_REPROBES budget is local to each onUsageLimit invocation. dispatch-role.mjs re-dispatches a resumed member with attempt -= 1, so repeated clear-then-refail cycles have no overall cap on pause time. An exhausted wait throws UsageLimitWaitExhaustedError straight out of the ladder, with no degrade, and it is a typed sprint abort.

entries.title: Raw sync/push primitives may only be called from git-sync.mjs; everyone else must use createGitSync's bracketed entry points
entries.summary: unbracketed-push-guard.mjs scans every guarded fleet-sprint module and flags any bare call of doltPushAfter, syncMemberAfter, DoltSync.syncBefore or DoltSync.syncAfter outside git-sync.mjs (UNBRACKETED_PUSH_EXEMPT) and the two sanctioned wrapper bodies syncMemberAfterOrdered and verifyDoerStreakClosed. New code must go through withGitSync, syncBeadsBefore/After, pushBeadsAfter or pushGitAfter.

entries.title: Use normalizeMsysPathForPlatform (in dolt-orphan-sweep.mjs) before path.resolve on Git-Bash-sourced paths
entries.summary: On win32, path.resolve('/c/Users/x') yields C:\c\Users\x; normalizeMsysPathForPlatform rewrites a /<drive>/... MSYS path to <DRIVE>:\... (no-op on other platforms or native paths). It lives in packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/dolt-orphan-sweep.mjs and is reused by bin/serve.mjs (FLEET_SE_SWEEP_OWNER_DATA_DIR) and backlog-member.mjs.

entries.title: Dolt mutex sprintId+pid does not identify one pusher: all D-pushes in a sprint process share both
entries.summary: doltPushAfter acquires the supervisor dolt mutex with (sprintId || member, {pid: process.pid}), so concurrent member D-pushes inside one sprint process present identical sprintId and pid; any mutex logic that treats {sprintId,pid} as one client identity breaks mutual exclusion.

entries.title: dolt-orphan-sweep filters AND kills inside the generated shell string; JS only reports
entries.summary: buildSweepCommand embeds the port range, age bound, optional --data-dir owner filter and the kill itself (Stop-Process / xargs kill -9) into one PowerShell or ps|awk command; sweepOnce only parses ORPHAN: lines and logs them as killed with no JS-side re-check. A dropped owner argument or filter bug is only caught by tests that inspect or execute the generated command.

entries.title: git says (fetch first), not (non-fast-forward), when the diverging remote tip was never fetched
entries.summary: A rejected push reports (non-fast-forward) only after the remote tip has been fetched; before that git says (fetch first). The diverged classification for that common case therefore relies on the [rejected], 'failed to push some refs' and 'updates were rejected' patterns in generic-git.mjs DIVERGED, so narrowing them to /non-fast-forward/ would misclassify it.

entries.title: A nested node --test child silently no-ops unless NODE_TEST_CONTEXT is stripped from its env
entries.summary: node --test sets NODE_TEST_CONTEXT on its own process; a child spawned with it still present returns empty stdout and exit 0 without running anything, so any nested-suite gate must delete it and then assert a non-zero '# pass' count.

entries.title: A runner.js back-import is safe for hoisted function declarations but TDZ-unsafe for const values read at module-load time
entries.summary: member-sync.mjs and beads-children.mjs back-import resolveSettleShell from runner.js safely because it is a hoisted function declaration called only at runtime. A const read at module-evaluation time is not safe to back-import through the runner.js <-> module cycle (TDZ), so kb.mjs defines its own ROLE_DOER/ROLE_REVIEWER via kbRoleConst over contracts.ROLES for KB_SELF_INJECTING_ROLES (a frozen Set built at load) instead of reusing runner.js's module-private ROLE_DOER.

entries.title: Naming a test file mock-sprint-* enrolls it in phase3's nested run and real-bd budget
entries.summary: phase3-dispatch-engine-completeness.test.mjs finds test/mock-sprint-*.test.mjs by filename prefix at runtime. Every match is run again in a nested node --test child, and the match count (ASSUMED_MOCK_SPRINT_FILE_COUNT) feeds REAL_BD_NESTED_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS. So the filename alone decides whether a file joins that gate and its timeout budget.

entries.title: No dispatched command in the develop-injection mock sprint may contain '$(' or a backtick
entries.summary: test/mock-sprint-develop-injection.test.mjs fails if ANY command in its scenario commandLog contains '$(' or a backtick (plus the rejected payload snippets), so engine code must never interpolate LLM-supplied newTask text into a command string: titles are validated/sanitized by validateNewTask and descriptions go via bd create --body-file.

entries.title: strategy.execCommand resolves on non-zero exit (and maps a null exit code to 0); it rejects only on timeout, spawn/connection error or abort
entries.summary: LocalStrategy and RemoteStrategy (ssh.ts execCommand) resolve {stdout, stderr, code} regardless of exit status, so callers must branch on result.code; a throw means inactivity/max-total timeout, spawn/connection error or client abort. Both finalize with code ?? 0, so a process that ends with a null exit code (e.g. killed by a signal) resolves as code 0.

entries.title: bd list --parent excludes closed issues by default; use the documented --all flag to include them
entries.summary: bd list (including --parent <id>) drops closed issues unless --all is passed, so any child-counting or floor-seeding logic must pass --all or it undercounts / resets to zero once children close (computeChildFloor does). parent-notes-staleness.mjs collectParentNotesStalenessNotes still lists children with plain `bd list --parent <id> --json`, so its most-recent-child comparison never sees closed children.

entries.title: unattended has different read and write value shapes across list_members and update_member
entries.summary: list_members/member_detail emit unattended as false | 'auto' | 'dangerous' (boolean false, not the string), while update_member's schema is z.enum(['false','auto','dangerous']) behind a preprocess that maps boolean false to 'false', and the handler stores 'false' back as boolean false. The shell-ui models the read and write shapes as two distinct types (FleetMemberFields vs UpdateMemberBody).

entries.title: Develop dispatch excludes below-goal ready beads unless they block in-goal work or were worked on
entries.summary: runner.js dispatchableReadyLeafBeads filters readyLeafBeads through partitionReadyByGoal: a finite-priority below-goal bead is dropped unless it transitively blocks an open in-goal bead or is in workedOnBeadIds; there is deliberately no in-goal-ancestor exemption.

entries.title: Any supervisor ledger write before start() overwrites the on-disk ledger
entries.summary: createLedger's transact() persists the in-memory reservations map and has no 'loaded' guard; until ledger.start() (run by supervisor.start()) loads the file that map is empty, so claim/release/setScopeFreshness before start would write an empty reservations map over the real ledger. bin/serve.mjs therefore kicks the beads view's first refresh only after supervisor.start().

entries.title: macOS fleet-supervisor stop boots the job out, so start()'s kickstart cannot bring it back
entries.summary: MacOSServiceManager.stop for services without gracefulStopViaServerJson (the fleet-supervisor) runs launchctl bootout, which unloads the job; start() only runs launchctl kickstart (no re-bootstrap) and isInstalled() just checks the plist file exists. So apra-fleet stop followed by start/restart leaves the supervisor down on macOS (startSupervisorServiceIfInstalled only warns, or throws in strict mode) until register() re-bootstraps it.

entries.title: reservedBy is the string mirror of Agent.reservation and member-reservation.ts is its only writer
entries.summary: Readers outside member-reservation.ts and list-members.ts still read the reservedBy string, so the two fields must always be written and cleared in the same updateAgent call; any site that clears one alone would make getReservation report a phantom holder.

entries.title: Doer retry reset salvages local work to a fleet-salvage side ref and fails closed
entries.summary: When withGitSync runs with resumeOntoRemoteTip, syncMemberBefore(resetToRemoteTip) first calls salvageBeforeReset, which pins unpublished commits and tracked uncommitted edits (via git stash create) on a local, never-pushed fleet-salvage/<branch-slug>/<sha12> ref without moving the sprint branch; untracked files are excluded. Any salvage failure throws GitSyncError and the git reset --hard is skipped.

entries.title: bd show <missing-id> exits 1, so the child-id collision probe's catch branch is the normal free-id path
entries.summary: bd show <missing> --json exits non-zero printing {"error":"no issues found ..."}; FleetWorkflow.command() turns a non-zero structuredContent.exitCode into a CommandError carrying the raw output on details.text. assertChildIdFree therefore lands in its catch on every free id and relies on classifyBdShowProbeError parsing details.text (fallback err.message) to return 'absent'; anything else is 'unknown' and fails closed. Any new existence probe through command() must classify the error the same way.

entries.title: run-tests.mjs default run only picks top-level test/*.test.mjs and isolates heavy suites via a registry
entries.summary: With no file argument, scripts/run-tests.mjs readdirs only test/ (non-recursive), runs everything at TEST_CONCURRENCY except files listed in test/helpers/serial-process-suites.mjs, which run afterwards at concurrency 1 within the same shared deadline. A new heavy real-process test file must be registered there, and a stale entry fails the run loudly.

entries.title: A new role-policies budget name must also be added to runner.js's budgets map and the test harness, or resolveBudget throws
entries.summary: role-policies.mjs names timeouts symbolically (e.g. budgets('DISPATCH_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_S', 'DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_S')), and dispatch-role.mjs resolveBudget throws when ctx.budgets lacks the name. The map comes from runner.js's dispatchRole ctx `budgets: {...}` and, in tests, from createRecordingCtx's default budgets in test/helpers/dispatch-role-harness.mjs (with exported sentinel constants), so a new or renamed budget must change all three files together or any dispatch of that row throws at dispatch time.

entries.title: member-provisioning.mjs and coordination.mjs are barred from any includes/match/toLowerCase call
entries.summary: test/phase5-consumer-migration-end-state.test.mjs fails if any line (comments included) of fleet-sprint/member-provisioning.mjs or fleet-sprint/coordination.mjs matches /\.includes\(|\.match\(|\.toLowerCase\(\)/, even for an Array membership check. It also fails if readMemberVcsCredentialToken or parseExpiresAtFromProvisionText appears in any .mjs/.js file under fleet-sprint/ (docs/ and skills/ excluded). Use Set.has, regex .test() or structured status fields instead.

entries.title: Console cookie on GET /ui is issued only to loopback socket peers, fail closed
entries.summary: handleConsoleRequest sets the apra_console_token cookie only when isLoopbackRemoteAddress(req.socket.remoteAddress) is true; a fake request with no socket gets no cookie, so tests needing the cookie must set socket.remoteAddress.

entries.title: Tests delegating to the shared vcs_credential_exec simulator get its fixed tokens, not their own
entries.summary: defaultMockCallTool's vcs_credential_exec branch substitutes the module-private MOCK_VCS_CREDENTIAL_TOKENS ('mock-vcs-module-token' for github, 'mock-azure-devops-pat' for azure-devops), so a test that delegates to it but asserts on its own token literal either goes red or keeps a no-leak assertion that can never fail (e.g. vcs-auth-pr-self-heal.test.mjs's assertNoRawTokenInLogs defaults to 'mock-vcs-module-pr-token').

entries.title: The success-path terminal record is runSprintCycle's return value, persisted by the workflow viewer
entries.summary: publishState('terminal', ...) is called only on failure paths (runner.js's abort handler and fatal-diagnostics.mjs). On success the workflow viewer's end handler stores the script's return value wholesale as state.result and moves running/<runId>.json to old_runs/<runId>.json, so a new field returned from runSprintCycle reaches the terminal record without a separate write.

entries.title: Member fleet install never overwrites an unmarked existing install; only opt-in replace-full does, decided before the up-to-date gates
entries.summary: ensureOnce in member-fleet-install.ts treats an existing apra-fleet binary without the member-install marker as a possible human full install and never installs --member over it. The only exception is fleet_install replace-full (ensureMemberFleetInstall opts.replaceFull), which probes the marker BEFORE the version short-circuits (so a same-version full install is replaced too) and calls replaceFullInstall only on a clean 'absent' marker answer; a probe-failed marker refuses with no destructive command.

entries.title: doltPullBefore records the remote tip before the caller re-lists, so a failed post-pull list is not retried
entries.summary: doltPullBefore records the new remote tip as soon as the pull succeeds. A caller that skips its re-list on remote-unchanged must also track whether its own last list succeeded; otherwise a list failure after a successful pull leaves stale data marked fresh.

entries.title: A failed last-cycle deploy forces the sprint verdict to FAIL in the orchestrator, not the LLM
entries.summary: runner.js keeps lastDeployFailure for the latest cycle. Both satisfied exits (root-closed and goal-priority) refuse to fire while it is set and re-attempt the deploy, bounded by maxCycles and DEPLOY_RETRY_CYCLE_LIMIT. Final Review then overrides any PASS to FAIL with a reason naming the cycle and deployer notes.

entries.title: SEA binary bundles workspace packages, so staleness inputs must include them
entries.summary: scripts/build-sea.mjs bundles src/index.ts with esbuild bundle:true and only cpu-features external, so imported workspace packages (fleet-api-contract, apra-fleet-client) are baked into the SEA binary and any freshness check must include their sources.

entries.title: compose_permissions denylist patterns match a normalized form where only the FIRST colon becomes a space
entries.summary: normalizePermission() does replace(':', ' ') without a global flag, so host:port only collapses to 'host port' when no earlier colon appears in the payload -- a real evasion for space-bearing patterns.
